precepts.text: The word of God is quick, meaning alive, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. The word of God will cut you deeply, to the deepest part of your thought process, and if you have never felt that cut in class, examine yourself. Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do. If you are tethered to Christ, you are tethered to wisdom, and you will know the intention of the heart of a person when they speak.
precepts.point: For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty. That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2. If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern, so you understand why people do the things they do, so you know the intents of a person's heart when they speak.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Wisdom “is the breath of the power of God.” The power of God is the word of God, and the word of God is wisdom. They're all synonymous; they all mean the same thing. The word of God is this book, and the word of God is Christ. It is one pureness, one avenue, with no variableness in what it means. That is why the Christian church has destroyed the minds of a people, making them believe you can separate Christ from the commandments. He is the word. You can't believe on Christ and not keep the commandments, and you can't keep the commandments and not believe on Christ. It's an oxymoron. Yet the witchcraft called Christianity has separated them to the point that it has been said that if you keep the commandments, you're sinning. Your church made you dumb as hell.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Quick means alive. This word is alive; it's not like a textbook. It will affect you to the deepest part of your thought process. It cuts, until you feel sick to your stomach, an emptiness like hunger. If you have never felt that cut in class, examine yourself.

“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” If you are tethered to Christ, you have to be tethered to wisdom, and if you are tethered to Christ and to wisdom, you know BS when you hear it. You know the intention of the heart of a person when they speak. You hear the pity party you've heard a thousand times before. You tell a man, stop talking, and he keeps talking, explaining, digging the ditch deeper, thinking he's making sense and embarrassing himself. A spiritual man discerneth all things. We could be wrong, we're not 100% with everything, we're learning ourselves; but for the most part, tethered to wisdom, you understand false speech.

precepts.text: For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, a city is builded, and rest is allowed. Spoken to Israel, not to all nations.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“For we which have believed do enter into rest.” What is that rest that is promised? Ezra shows it: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom.”

This paradise is spoken to the Israelites. It is not talking about all nations. Paradise opened, the tree of life planted, a city builded and rest allowed: that is what is left to us, the promise “of entering into his rest.”

“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them.” The gospel did not begin in the book of Matthew; Christ was taught to our forefathers too. But “the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” They disobeyed Christ and were moved with unbelief, and their unbelief is what kept them from entering in. “Let us therefore fear”, then, lest any of us come short of the paradise and the rest that is allowed to Israel.

precepts.text: Thou leddest Adam into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward. Paradise was already here before the foundation of the earth; that is the rest prepared from the foundation of the world.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Paul says God’s works “were finished from the foundation of the world.” The rest is not something new; it was prepared before anything else was. Ezra shows it: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.”

Paradise was here before the earth came forth. Before Christ said the evening and the morning were the first day, paradise was already here. That is the paradise opened to Israel in 2 Esdras 8:52, where the tree of life is planted and rest is allowed.

So when Hebrews says the works were finished from the foundation of the world, it is telling you the rest was already created and waiting. Then “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” That number seven keeps coming back: the seventh day Sabbath points to that rest God prepared from the beginning.

precepts.text: Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail. No matter what we are going through, we must be in pain and do this work to bring forth the kingdom.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Paul is making a comparison between our works and God’s. God worked, then rested; so must we. Micah shows the labour: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city.”

No matter what we are going through, brothers and sisters, we have to be in pain and do this work. Be in pain to bring forth the kingdom of heaven on earth.

That is why Paul says “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” Labour, labour in pain, bring forth your works to enter into that rest, which is the kingdom. Rest is entered by labour. The generation in the wilderness fell because of unbelief; the daughter of Zion must travail to bring forth.

precepts.text: Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them. Your works are what follow you through those gates.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Revelation shows who rests and why: “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.”

They rest from their labours, and their works follow them. Your works are what are going to allow you to enter in through those gates. The rest is not handed to the idle; it comes after the labour, and the labour goes with you into it.

So “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief” that we read of in the wilderness. Labour in pain, bring forth your works, like the daughter of Zion in travail, and then rest from those labours in the kingdom.

precepts.text: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel; the strangers shall be joined to the house of Jacob, and Israel shall rule over their oppressors. And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve. That is the true rest: after the Sabbath we go back to labouring in Esau's system Monday morning, but that day ends the bondage itself.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The seventh day Sabbath, resting from our servile work, is a similitude the Most High uses for us resting in the kingdom when it is established. That is the true rest, when we will really rest from servile work. Because after the Sabbath some of us have to go to work on Sunday, then Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, slaving for Esau.

Isaiah shows the day of that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.” The nations are going to be joined with us, but how? “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” They are our possession.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” That is the true rest: rest from our sorrow, from our fear, and from the hard bondage we were made to serve.

That is why “if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.” That Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the Hamites, but we did not get true rest in the land; there were enemies on all sides, the Amalekites and the Hamites we were fighting. The true rest is the kingdom of God on earth, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.”

precepts.text: Be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years. The seventh day maps to the thousand years.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” Peter shows how that seventh day reaches forward to the kingdom: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.”

One day with the Lord, brothers, is a thousand years. So the seventh day is not only the Sabbath we keep each week; it maps to a thousand years, the reign that comes after the heavens and earth that are now are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment.

That is why “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” The rest of the seventh day is the similitude, and the thousand years is the substance: the day we reign with Christ, as Revelation 20:4 shows.

precepts.text: And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting and reigning with Christ; that is what every seventh day is rehearsing.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
If one day with the Lord is a thousand years, what is the seventh day rest? Revelation shows it: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

They lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. That is going into the rest. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting with Christ, and every seventh day is rehearsing it.

The rest promised in Hebrews is not the land Joshua brought us into, and not only the one day a week before going back to labour in Esau’s system. It is the eternal reign with Christ when he comes back, sitting on thrones with judgment given to us, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Seven represents completion, and the seventh day points to that completion: the kingdom and the thousand years with Christ.

precepts.text: Labor to enter into that rest. The word of God is quick and powerful and a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. The power of God is his word, which is wisdom, and it governs the intents where sin begins.
precepts.point: In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 says wisdom is “the breath of the power of God.” What is the power of God? Hebrews 4 answers.

“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” We fought that example of unbelief. If we believe, we are tethered with God and following wisdom. Wisdom is pure, steadfast and sure, and we enter into that rest.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful.” Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 just said wisdom is “quick”, and “having all power.” The same words. And it is “sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”

The intents of the heart are where sin begins. So we want that pure influence, so that the intents of this mind are not led astray and what guides and directs us is the word of God. There should be something in all of us that says, I can’t do that, it is wrong to do that. If we turn aside from that, we are saying we are hypocrites and don’t really believe. God has chosen us, for whatever reason, to give us wisdom. The power of God is the word of God. It is wisdom.

precepts.text: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life. You cannot fight that fight without holding to your profession.
precepts.point: There is no perfect sister; this is a hospital and all of us are sick, and Christ came for those who admit it. Sisters who complain that another sister has an attitude need a solution, not a grievance, and patience. And when you fall, get back up; the righteous fall seven times. Where would you go, back to white Jesus? Leaders, do not kick a brother when he is down or take revenge on a brother who lost rank; build him back up.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
“Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.” What is our profession? We are prophets, and a prophet’s profession is to teach. All of us are supposed to be teachers. Timothy gives the charge: “Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.”

You cannot get that eternal life if you do not hold on to your profession. How are you going to fight the good fight of faith if you are not holding on to it? Your profession is to go out there and wake up our people. Your profession is to put in work, because faith without works is dead. Your first work is supposed to be in this truth, not your job. The minute we say profession, some think we mean I’m a nurse, I’m a doctor. No.

What good is it for a prophet to do nothing with it? Some of you never travel, never leave the state of Georgia, yet you say I’m a prophet. All Israel is not in Georgia; Israel is scattered to the four corners of the earth. How many of you prophets have a valid passport? Brothers have had passports since they were three. If you don’t have one, you should be ashamed. Get a passport; Donald Trump is going to force you to get one too. We have much work to do.

And “all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” God will bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or evil. So hold fast the profession, fight the fight, and lay hold on eternal life with a high priest who was “in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.”

precepts.text: Thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven.
precepts.point: Those who believe enter into rest, and those who did not believe were kept out.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” We want God's kingdom to be in earth as it is in heaven, and that is what we are praying for right now: the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

This ties to the rest of Hebrews 4. When Genesis says God “rested on the seventh day from all his work”, it does not mean God was tired and went to get some sleep. Moses is an analogy, a similitude. Hebrews says “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day”: God's rest is a place, paradise. 2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was planted before the earth, and leading Adam into paradise is entering into his rest.

That is the kingdom of Adam. When Adam had dominion on the earth, it was on a much higher level than people think. Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth, the only flesh, him and his wife, that could, until he committed sin; flesh and blood cannot be up there because of that sinful nature. How Adam was on the earth is basically how we are going to be in the future, the difference being that he was not in the flesh as we are. So when we pray “Thy kingdom come”, we are praying for what was once on the earth in Adam's day to be on the earth again.

precepts.text: As the days of heaven upon the earth.
precepts.point: Those who believe enter into rest, and those who did not believe were kept out.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” What does Moses mean? When you go into the land and keep the commandments, it will be as the days of heaven upon the earth.

Moses saw Adam's kingdom. That is why he could say that going into the land and keeping the laws would be as the kingdom of heaven upon the earth. The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam was ruling.

So the promise of Hebrews 4:1, “a promise being left us of entering into his rest”, is the same promise: heaven's days upon the earth again. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Those to whom the word was first preached “entered not in because of unbelief”, “For we which have believed do enter into rest”. The one who has entered into his rest has “ceased from his own works”: the works are our labouring in this earth to bring forth the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.text: The holy city coming down from God out of heaven.
precepts.point: Those who believe enter into rest, and those who did not believe were kept out.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” Remember, it withdrew itself; now it is coming back.

2 Esdras 7:26 says it: “the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth.” That bride withdrawn from the earth is the holy city Jerusalem, the access to the spirit realm, which withdrew itself from the earth. For it to be withdrawn from the earth it must once have been on the earth, and it was, during the time of Adam. Adam was not running around butt naked; Adam was going back and forth to a spiritual realm.

The city is described with twelve gates for the twelve tribes of Israel and no heathens. So the tribes were around back then, and Adam went through a gate, the Judah gate. The twelve tribes around in the beginning were called the sons of God; Moses did not name them because the Lord said to hide these things. Jacob, Esau, will never go through those gates. They may stand outside and look at it and drop some stuff off in front of it, but they will never enter into those gates.

The city was prepared from the foundation of the world; it is already built, from the beginning. It is the rest God entered, the paradise Adam was led into, and the promise of Hebrews 4:1 that we must not come short of.

precepts.text: Fear lest ye come short as the fathers did: the gospel was preached unto them as unto us, but the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
precepts.point: The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. But the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith; they had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. They had the word, the laws, the miracles, and the Lord going before them “in fire by night, to shew you by what way ye should go, and in a cloud by day.” And “Yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God”.

That is the amazing part of this history: they saw all the miracles and were carried like a son, and still believed the Lord was setting them up to be killed by giants, when a giant has nothing on the Most High. The word did not profit them because it was not mixed with faith. They had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

So “Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.” The same promise is left to us, and the same way of coming short is open to us: hearing the word and not mixing it with faith.

precepts.text: The gospel was preached unto them in the wilderness as it is preached unto us: keep the commandments and inherit the kingdom prepared for Israel; under Christ the difference is an eternal reign, with our spirit changed so we cannot transgress.
precepts.point: This is the same word the Lord foretold to Moses that Joshua now fulfills. The promised land was meant to be as the days of heaven upon the earth, and the condition was diligently keeping all the commandments, to love the Lord, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; then the Lord would drive out nations greater and mightier than Israel. Heaven was never about everybody being equal and holding hands; heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations, and that has always been the gospel.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” The gospel was preached unto them in the wilderness as it is preached unto us: keep the commandments and inherit the kingdom prepared for Israel.

That is what the Lord was telling Joshua: every place the sole of your foot treads, from the wilderness and Lebanon unto the great river Euphrates and unto the great sea, is given to the children of Israel. Heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations; it has always been the gospel. Under Christ the difference is an eternal reign, with our spirit changed so we cannot transgress. The word did not profit them because it was not mixed with faith; let it profit us.

precepts.text: Let us come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need; we go straight to Christ our high priest.
precepts.point: Oh that I knew where I might find him, that I might come even to his seat. I would order my cause before him and fill my mouth with arguments. Job wants to bring his case straight to God's seat.

note.label: Job 23: I Shall Come Forth As Gold

precepts.why:
Job's complaint is bitter and his stroke is heavier than his groaning, and he says, “Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.” He wants to bring his case straight to God's seat.

We have that seat: “Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.” We go straight to Christ our high priest. What Job longed for, to come even to his seat and order his cause before him, we do boldly at the throne of grace, and there we obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
The twoedged sword that John saw. “For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword,” So when John saw the twoedged sword come out of his mouth, it is making reference to the scriptures, the word of God.

“piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit,” That is why when we teach brothers, when we teach sisters, we must use the words of God, the words in the Bible. You might think his words don't have any effect, but whoever hears his word, it is cutting them like a twoedged sword. God says his word does damage. When they walk by saying you're full of crap, the Bible's garbage, just use one word: Esau. You know what they are going to do? Look it up. Esau is a devout believer in research; they have books, they have dictionaries, and they pride their children on knowing everything. You wear a shirt that says something, the only one that pays attention to it is Esau: reading it, Googling it on the phone. That is what they do.

“and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” That is why when you make judgments, use the scriptures. Bring out the laws of God; that is going to cut people.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword. So the word of God is quick and powerful and sharper than any two-edged sword that we can manufacture, see or purchase.
Piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow. So this word of God, this sword, is able to divide soul and spirit.

And is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. So the word of God causes discernment. Now this is very important. Remember I made mention earlier that you have to line your actions up with the word of God. But the Bible says the word of God will show you what your intentions really are. So it discerns where your thoughts lie. Are your thoughts godly or are your thoughts wicked?

And what your intentions really are. Perfect example, in Sirach it tells you about beware of a counsellor, and know what need he has of thee. So if you want a counsellor, and hypothetically that counsellor is a lustful man, and you want to ask him about a sister, about marriage. Would that counsellor counsel for your benefit? No, he is going to counsel for himself. The same thing with a thief. Do not go to a thief and ask him about investment options or how to manage your money. What is his counsel going to be? Beneficial to you or to him? So you have to know what a counsellor's intentions are.

But the word of God gives that same ability to you about yourself. We can easily use the word of God for somebody else. We are experts in using the word of God to discern the thoughts and intents of somebody else. But when it is ourselves, it is extremely difficult. Hence the topic today.

What I want you to see is that bitterness does not travel alone. Bitterness is not the lonely traveller, where that is the only transgression you will have to be dealing with. There are other contributing factors. There are other things that you are battling with. There is other rebelliousness within you. And then the bitterness is just the icing on the cake.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: the gospel did not begin in Matthew; it was preached to our forefathers, and it did not profit them, not being mixed with faith.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: For if Jesus had given them rest: that Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the nations of Canaan, but there were enemies on every side, so the land was not the true rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God: the seventh day Sabbath is the similitude, and the substance is the kingdom, reigning with Christ.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: All things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do. Let us hold fast our profession: we are prophets, and a prophet's profession is to teach and wake up our people. Faith without works is dead, and your first work is this truth, not your job.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: We have a high priest touched with the feeling of our infirmities, tempted in all points yet without sin. Christ understands the fight, so nobody has the excuse that the leaders do not understand. Taking a break from the brotherhood only makes you worse.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: God did not rest because he was tired. Entering his rest means entering paradise.
Those who believe enter into rest, and those who did not believe were kept out.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

points: So the scripture says, let us what? Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest — that eternal rest — any of you should seem to come short of it. Any of you should come short of it. Any of you should come short of it.

So then you have got to sit back and examine, and ask yourself: Lord, where am I at in this truth? With my year in, my two years in, my five years in, my ten years in. You have got to self-examine. You have got to take spiritual inventory.
